title: Nabopolassar
summary: Founder of the Neo-Babylonian (Chaldean) dynasty, father of Nebuchadnezzar II.
description: Founder of the Neo-Babylonian (Chaldean) dynasty, father of Nebuchadnezzar II. Person record added by the CFAH pass for CFAH's reign dates; dates are as printed in the CFAH paper cited.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year.

standby.note: Standby placement only. Chronological Framework of Ancient History prints this BC/AD year on the reign entry (626/625 B.C.). It is not a sort year. No Anno Mundi, regnal length, or Julian Period figure was converted to obtain it.

reign.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 5: The Babylonian Dynasties of Berossus," ARJ 16 (2023): 635–670, section "AP-45: Dynasty 8: Neo-Babylonian Empire: 626–539 B.C."
reign.note: When Nabopolassar "took the kingship of Babylon away from Assyria".

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 88; Berossus, ap. Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: A footnote says "Nabopollasar, see p. 84." The p. 84 mention was not given a separate length in this pass.

reign.date: “our city was desolate during the interval of seventy years, until the days of Cyrus king of Persia”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 64; Berossus, ap. Josephus, Against Apion, book 1
reign.note: Josephus, Against Apion, book 1, chapter 19, as this page cites it. Nabopallasar sent Nabuchodonosor. No BC year is printed.

reign.date: “died in the city of Babylon, after he had reigned twenty-nine years”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 65; Berossus, ap. Josephus, Against Apion, book 1
reign.note: The father is Nabopollasar. Pass 1, p. 88, prints that Nabupalsar (Nabopollassar) reigned 20 years. Both are kept.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 84; Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: The parenthesis identifies Nabopollasar with Sardanapallus. The records were not merged. No new length is printed in this sentence.
